subject: copper
author: metals/claude-opus-5-5
question: how tight is copper and is the LME backwardation explained by stocks?

balance_view.text: Visible copper stocks (LME + SHFE) are 328,106 t [s34], the 43 percentile since 2014 [s35]: not low. SHFE is the tight venue: 36.8% below its 5-year same-week average [s36] after a 19,606 t weekly draw [s25], -1.36 sd against the seasonal norm [s26]. LME stocks of 273,750 t [s16] barely moved on the day (0.05 sd [s18]). COMEX stocks are not in the repo, so part of the picture is missing.

curve_shape.text: LME cash sits 1.016% over the 3-month price [s30]; adding the interest cost at a 4.04% T-bill [s31] gives 2.037% net of interest [s32], the 98 percentile of weekly history since 2014 [s33]. The storage fit (-0.673 pp per log unit of visible stocks [s37], t -5.28 [s38]) implies 0.308% at today's stocks [s39], so the net spread is 1.73 pp above it [s40], at the 99 percentile of the fit's residuals [s41].

positioning.text: COMEX managed money is at the 48.7179 percentile of three years [s5], down 4.8768 pp on the week [s6]. The trend proxy reads correction; the 21-day leg flips at 6.7185 [s7]. Context, not a signal.

narrative_stage.text: The news narrative 'China stimulus' carried 2 headlines against a prior daily average of 0.9 [s11] [s12]; its stage is insufficient coverage.

what_changed: First copper card: no earlier card to compare.
would_change_view: Visible stocks rising while the net spread stays above the inventory-implied level (the tightness would then be about invisible or COMEX metal, not shortage).
SHFE stocks back toward their 5-year same-week norm.
The LME cash premium falling back inside the range the storage fit implies.
inference: Read: the LME curve is far tighter than visible stocks explain. Candidates, none measured here: metal pulled into COMEX sheds (not in the repo), off-exchange or bonded Chinese stocks, or a concentrated holding of LME warrants. The fit is contemporaneous; it is not a forecast that the spread will close.

Read: a big SHFE draw is not, on its own, a price event: COMEX copper shows no measurable reaction to SHFE stock surprises (0.0003% per sd [s27], t 0.0041 [s28]). LME surprises do line up with same-day moves (-0.1621% per sd [s19], t -6.8045 [s20]), with part of it the next day (-0.083% [s23]).
open_questions: COMEX warehouse stocks are not reachable (the CME blocks scripts): they would test the COMEX-pull reading.
